questions.stem: Calculate the definite integral ∫[2,∞] e^(-x) dx.
questions.explanation: The integral of e^(-x) is -e^{-x}. Evaluate at the limits of integration and subtract.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to forget to evaluate the antiderivative at infinity, which results in -e^{-∞} = 0.

questions.stem: Find the value of ∫[0,∞] e^(-x) dx.
questions.explanation: The integral of e^(-x) is -e^{-x}. Evaluate at the limits of integration and subtract.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to think that ∫[0,∞] e^(-x) dx diverges, but it actually converges to 1.
